c.tagline: West Lake serenity and Alibaba ambition, wrapped in tea hills and canals.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares start around ¥13 for the first 3 km; most locals summon cabs and pay via Didi or Alipay/WeChat rather than hailing on the street or using cash.

emergency.note: Police 110, ambulance 120, fire 119. The 12345 city hotline handles general help; foreign-language assistance is limited, so translation apps help.

avoid.reason: Beware 'tea ceremony' and art-student scams targeting tourists around West Lake, and watch for pickpockets in dense holiday crowds.

hood_desc: The scenic heart of the city wrapped around West Lake (Xihu), with causeways, tea houses, pagodas, and Lingyin Temple nearby; best for first-timers who want Hangzhou's iconic sights within easy reach.

Downtown Hangzhou around Wulin Square and Hubin, the city's main commercial and shopping core with department stores, malls, restaurants, and a metro interchange; suits travelers who want a central, well-connected base.

A modern high-tech district on the south bank of the Qiantang River, home to riverside parks, corporate campuses, and newer residential towers; suits business travelers and those wanting quieter, contemporary surroundings.

A dense inner-city area straddling the southern end of the Grand Canal near Wulin and the Gongchen Bridge, mixing old canal-side lanes with markets and local eateries; good for travelers wanting an authentic, everyday-life feel.

The Future Sci-Tech City in Yuhang, anchored by Alibaba's campus and the Xixi Wetland, a spread-out zone of tech offices, resorts, and green space; suits business visitors and those linked to the tech scene rather than sightseers.
lodging: Four Seasons Hotel Hangzhou at West Lake
Mingtown Hangzhou West Lake International Youth Hostel
Sheraton Grand Hangzhou Wetland Park Resort
Vienna Hotel Hangzhou Future Sci-Tech City

water.note: Stick to bottled or boiled water; avoid tap water and ice made from it.

transit.hours: Metro runs roughly 6:00 AM to 11:00 PM; city buses run from early morning until around 10-11 PM with a few late-night lines.
transit.note: Hangzhou has an extensive and still-expanding metro network (a dozen-plus lines) that reaches West Lake, the train stations, and the airport, backed by a dense bus network and ubiquitous shared bikes.
transit.pay: Pay by scanning Alipay/WeChat QR or the Hangzhou transit QR at metro gates and on buses; a rechargeable transit card and single-journey metro tokens also work. Foreign visitors typically link a card inside Alipay. Metro fares are distance-based (¥2-8).

bus: Intercity coaches to other Zhejiang and Yangtze Delta cities

car.idp: Not valid (a Chinese driving license is required to drive)

ferry: Grand Canal water bus (公交水上巴士) commuter service
train: Hangzhou East Railway Station (major high-speed rail hub)

transit.m: Metro Line 7 to city center (~50-60 min, direct from terminal)
Airport shuttle bus to downtown Wulin/train stations (~60 min)
Taxi to city center (40-60 min depending on traffic)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary or expected; restaurants do not add service charge and rounding up is unnecessary.
